title: Meet the IonQ Federal Advisory Board
summary: Mission owners and program office leaders have pressing questions about quantum implementation that many vendors aren’t ready to answer: Far beyond the physics of quantum, these leaders are asking where they need quantum first, how to run a successful pilot, and how to plan for cryptographic migration.
body_markdown:
Mission owners and program office leadershave pressing questions about quantum implementation that many vendors aren’tready to answer: Far beyond the physics of quantum, these leaders are askingwhere they need quantum first, how to run a successful pilot, and how to planfor cryptographic migration.


The eight members of IonQ Federal'sAdvisory Board have spent their careers on exactly those questions. Betweenthem, they have held leadership positions at the National Security Agency, theDefense Intelligence Agency, DARPA, Army Futures Command, U.S. Cyber Command,the Office of Space Commerce, and federal defense contractors.


The board exists to ensure IonQ understandscustomer needs, anticipates their challenges, and produces solutions built withfederal missions in mind.


## What is the FederalAdvisory Board?


The IonQ Federal Advisory Board is anindependent, non-governing group of senior leaders who advise IonQ on servingU.S. and allied defense and intelligence customers. Members provide theircandid, independent counsel and hold no managing stake in the company.


The board reports to IonQ Federal ExecutiveChairman Robert Cardillo and is chaired by George Barnes, former DeputyDirector of the National Security Agency. Members meet several times a year toreview IonQ’s strategy and product direction. Each serves a one-year term,renewable by mutual agreement.


Members are chosen for experience acrossdefense and intelligence policy, technology, and operations; for the range ofagencies, services, and disciplines they represent; and for their assessment ofwhere the national security landscape is heading.


## Why the BoardExists


IonQ Federal was formed to delivertrapped-ion quantum computing, quantum sensing, quantum networking, andquantum-safe security to national security missions. Moving those capabilitiesfrom research engagements into fielded systems raises questions that governmentcustomers face every day, but a technical roadmap does not answer.


The board was formed to keep IonQ close tothe customer, allowing us to anticipate their needs and respond withmission-ready solutions. The board also reflects what we think governmentdecision-makers will expect of any frontier technology vendor.


## Meet the Members


### George Barnes,Chair


*Former Deputy Director, National SecurityAgency*


George Barnes served as Deputy Director andsenior civilian leader of the National Security Agency from April 2017 throughSeptember 2023, capping a 36-year career at the agency. As NSA's chiefoperating officer, he oversaw strategy, policy, and operations, and positionedthe agency as an integrated mission partner across the U.S. defense andintelligence enterprise. He is now President of Red Cell Partners' CyberPractice and a Partner at the firm.


### LTG Robert (Bob) P. Ashley Jr.,USA (Ret.)


*Former Director, Defense IntelligenceAgency*


Bob Ashley is a retired Army lieutenantgeneral and career intelligence officer with 36 years of active-duty service.He served as the 21st Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, as theArmy's senior intelligence officer, and as commandant of the Army IntelligenceCenter and School, where he led the training of more than 10,000 soldiers ayear. He deployed for several years as a brigade and squadron commander inAfghanistan and Iraq and as the senior intelligence officer for multiplecommands.


### Gerard (Gerry) A. Fasano


*Former Chief Growth Officer, Leidos*


Gerry Fasano is a board director and formercorporate officer with more than four decades of experience leading and scalingdefense and technology enterprises. He retired as Chief Growth Officer ofLeidos, where he led enterprise-wide teams across business development,capture, government affairs, communications, and strategy after serving asPresident of the Leidos Defense Group. Before Leidos, he led Lockheed Martin'sInformation Systems & Global Solutions Business Development and Mergers& Acquisitions organization and served as General Manager of its DefenseGroup.


### Gilbert (Gil) Herrera


*Former Director of Research, NationalSecurity Agency*


Gil Herrera is a nationally recognizedtechnical expert in quantum information science, microelectronics, and nationalsecurity research. Over a 45-year career in national laboratories, government,and the private sector, he served as Director of Research at the NationalSecurity Agency and spent nearly 40 years at Sandia National Laboratories,where his last assignment was Laboratory Fellow. He previously served with NSAon loan from Sandia as Director of the Laboratory for Physical Sciences.


### David P. Luber


*Former Director of Cybersecurity, NationalSecurity Agency*


Dave Luber served 38 years at the NationalSecurity Agency, culminating as Director of Cybersecurity and Deputy NationalManager for National Security Systems. His career spanned signals intelligenceand cybersecurity, including leadership within Tailored Access Operations asChief of the Remote Operations Center and Chief of Advanced Network Operations,and as Director of NSA Colorado. He also served as Executive Director of U.S.Cyber Command, the highest-ranking civilian position at USCYBERCOM. He is thefounder of Luber Cyber LLC.


### Gen. John M. (Mike) Murray, USA(Ret.)


*First Commanding General, U.S. Army FuturesCommand*


Mike Murray began his 40-year Army careerin 1982, commissioned as an infantry officer through The Ohio StateUniversity's Army ROTC program. In 2018, he became the first Commanding Generalof United States Army Futures Command, a new four-star command headquartered inAustin, Texas. His Pentagon assignments included Deputy Chief of Staff, G-8,and Director of Force Management. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, he served asa brigade combat team commander, as corps operations officer during the Surge,and as Deputy Commanding General of the 1st Cavalry Division. He also served asDeputy Commander for Support and Commander of Task Force 3 in Afghanistanduring Operations Enduring Freedom and Resolute Support.


### Kevin M. O'Connell


*Former Director, Office of Space Commerce,U.S. Department of Commerce*


Kevin O'Connell is CEO of Space EconomyRising, an advisory firm serving space companies, investors, and otherstakeholders in the space economy, and a recognized expert on space commerce,the global space economy, and U.S. national security. For almost four decades,he has focused on space commercialization and technological competitiveness.From 2018 to 2021, he directed the Office of Space Commerce at the U.S.Department of Commerce, serving as the principal U.S. government advocate forthe commercial space industry. His earlier career spanned the Department of Defense,the Department of State, the National Security Council, the Office of the VicePresident, the Office of the Director of Central Intelligence, and RANDCorporation.


### Steven H. Walker, PhD


*Former Director, DARPA; former CTO,Lockheed Martin*


Steve Walker is an independent consultantadvising industry, academia, and government on defense technology developmentand strategic innovation. He recently retired as Vice President and ChiefTechnology Officer of Lockheed Martin, where he was responsible for technologystrategy, internal R&D, strategic partnerships, and research laboratories,and stood up the Lockheed Martin AI Center. Before Lockheed Martin, he led theDefense Advanced Research Projects Agency from 2017 to 2020 after serving as DeputyDirector from 2013, developing new commercial space technologies,next-generation aircraft and missile prototypes, hypersonic glide and poweredpropulsion systems, mRNA vaccines, and AI-powered cybersecurity and spectrumdominance capabilities. He also served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of the AirForce for Science, Technology, and Engineering.


## Looking Ahead


The federal question about quantum hasshifted from whether it works to how it is bought, authorized, fielded, andsustained for the missions that need it. The Federal Advisory Board helps IonQapproach that question the way its customers do.
